newsitem.title: USA: Brooklyn Union reorganization plan approved.
newsitem.headline: Brooklyn Union reorganization plan approved.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co. said Wednesday its proposal to reorganize its gas distribution and other operations into a holding company was approved by the New York Public Service Commission.
The plan still needed approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission should not be a problem, the utility said, now that state regulators have cleared the proposal.

President Craig Matthews said in an interview that with the commission's approval, Brooklyn Union could go ahead with most of its plans, even if the holding company proposal is not accepted by shareholders.
The company expects to present the plan to shareholders at its annual meeting in February.
One of the changes approved by the commission allows the utility to offer additional services to customers.

Matthews said that possible new services include bill consolidation for property managers with more than one address in the company's service area and offering maintenance services on other than gas appliances.
Such service might have to be offered by a subsidiary other than the utility, he said, noting regulators' reluctance to allow regulated utilities to compete with other service providers.
Another possibility is energy use monitoring. Matthews said Brooklyn Union is now piloting a programme with Microsoft Corp. that automates thermostats, giving the user readings on a computer screen.

Brooklyn Union said the commision action allows the company to increase its non-utility investments significanty and that it expects to have 50 percent of profits from non-utility sources within five years.

Upon approval, the new holding company, to be named KeySpan Energy Corp., would trade in the New York Stock Exchange with the symbol KY. Brooklyn Union, the utility, will be the major subsidiary of the holding company.
